function: Joint learned user scheduling, BS active precoding and distributed RIS passive precoding (phase shifts) maximizing the ergodic sum rate approximation with statistical CSI (pp. 2, 7-8)
system: Downlink MU-MISO: BS with 8 antennas, 8 single-antenna users (2 scheduled), 2 distributed passive reflecting RISs of 64 elements, direct links blocked; band not stated (pp. 3, 9)
method: Multi-agent reinforcement learning: MAPPO with scheduling, BS precoding and RIS actors (fully connected, one hidden layer) and a centralized critic; offline centralized training, distributed execution (pp. 6-8, 10)
data_channel: Own simulator: Rician fading, path loss exponents 2.2 (BS-RIS) and 2.8 (RIS-user), Rician factor 6 dB, users random in a 6 m circle; 300 channel realizations (p. 9)
test_conditions: Trained at 10 dBm, Rician factor 6 dB, 8 users; tested at -5 to 25 dBm, -3 to 15 dB, 2 to 8 users (Figs. 7-8, pp. 10-12)
baselines: Non-learned: BFS-AO, BFS-PDS, random precoding, random RIS, round-robin. Learned: MADDPG of [1] (BFS-MADDPG, PPO-MADDPG, Random-MADDPG), PPO-AO (pp. 10, 13)
metrics: Ergodic sum rate (Monte Carlo, 300 channel realizations), performance ratio to BFS-AO, running time, Jain's fairness index (pp. 9-13)
complexity: MAPPO complexity order O((KM+MUL+NL+C(K,U))I+LI^2); running time 1.23 ms (N=64) vs 1957.21 ms for BFS-AO and 113.48 ms for PPO-AO (Table II, p. 13)
openness: none; no link to code or data and no release statement in the paper
q1_support: p. 3: "Rician fading channel model is adopted". The channels come from the authors' own Rician simulator with path loss exponents set on p. 9; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "trained at Kk,l = 6 dB is tested in other scenarios with". The Rician factor is varied from -3 to 15 dB (Fig. 7b); the network trained with K = 8 users is also applied with 2 to 8 actual users (Fig. 8a, p. 11).
q3_support: p. 10: "BFS-MADDPG: The optimal scheduling vector is obtained via BFS, while the trained MADDPG method in". [1] is the authors' earlier MADDPG paper (p. 3, Remark 1); non-learned BFS-AO, BFS-PDS and random precoding or RIS are compared on ergodic sum rate in Figs. 7-9 (pp. 11-12).
q4_support: p. 13: "we compare the running time of the above algorithms". Table II gives 1.23 ms for MAPPO against 1957.21 ms for BFS-AO at N = 64, and the order of complexity is stated on p. 8.
q5_support: p. 9: "300 independent channel realizations". Channels are generated by the authors' own simulator; the paper gives no link to code or data, uses no public dataset and makes no release statement.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv v1 (25 Oct 2024) of the MAPPO paper; the text does not print the DOI, so the match rests on the title and topic. Area 3: the agents set the BS precoder and the RIS phase shifts, and user scheduling is learned jointly with them, so above_phy does not apply. The carrier frequency is never stated. q2 counts the Rician-factor test and the test with fewer users than in training; the retrained cases for N, L and K (pp. 11-12) and the power sweep are not used for it.
